name: Mahmud’s household
goals: Keep court correspondence moving when authority is disputed.
Keep grain reaching the city without separating families on the quay.
bio: Mahmud’s seal can still open a door when his son’s orders arrive first. The household’s agents, dockworkers and boat crews do not owe their service on the same terms.
notes: fact: Brown describes Mahmud handing Ahmad his officers and regalia; Pires still calls Mahmud king in the 1511 deliberations (Brown ch. XXII, p. 166; Pires II, p. 280)
inference: Retainers clustered around patrons, but there is no secure roster of the royal port workforce (port-labour.md §§1–3)
gameplay: Bunga and Jernih bring distinct stories of enslavement and obligatory royal service into the household network; neither is an upgrade (port-labour.md §4)
